items.title: Linda's Head
items.note: Guitar songs that drift and smudge, on Grouper's own label. Quiet, strange and worth the full run.

items.title: Last Light of the Sun
items.note: Ambient, IDM, dub techno and a little drum and bass, with bamboo flute and typewriter in the mix. Soft on top, with real movement underneath.

items.title: Neram Pularumbol
items.note: Kerala drumming, drones and club bass, followed by a second half of remixes. Heavy in places, but it treats tradition as something alive.

items.title: Passing the Cup of Sorrows 1.1
items.note: The first piece from his album due 23 October. Tape-loop ambient, slow and sad.

items.title: Archives
items.note: Homemade instruments and chopped samples, built remotely between rural France and a London boat. The Quietus hears Autechre reworking The Wicker Man. Raw and odd.

items.title: SÖWT
items.note: Tenor saxophone drawing on Moroccan Gnawa tradition, set against blues-rooted jazz. A good one for a long evening.

items.title: Songs for Sad Poets Vol. III
items.note: Drone that breaks into short bursts out of long silence. Dark, patient and well suited to headphones.

items.title: Post Dub Cities
items.note: Austere dub-leaning electronics that sound like empty streets and wear. Cold and spare, in a good way.

items.title: Psychic Video
items.note: A preview from his DJ-Kicks mix, out 16 October. Dark, textured club music.

items.title: Shell and Core
items.note: Arabic-language post-rock and jazz, about lives left unfinished, like abandoned buildings.

items.title: Traces of Light
items.note: A saxophone quartet in quiet, searching post-bop, nine originals. The gentle pick of the week.

items.title: Alive Alone, Alive Together
items.note: Live guitar from four cities, fuzz and blues running through it, with Hamid Drake on drums for four tracks.
